title: Heuristic thread — spark notes (afternoon triage)
content:
Afternoon quick triage (spark notes)

Context:
- Spotted a small but repeatable quality regression on hosted-api model alias 'redwood-v1.10-quant' compared to v1.9.3 in production sampling for the small consumer chat workload (session length ~35 tokens).
- Regression surfaced in Canary run this morning (2025-02-12 09:12 PST) via the automated drift monitor; triage started ad-hoc.
- Quick goal: capture representative samples, apply a tiny ad-hoc rubric, see if this is a prompt/formatting sensitivity, model change, or quantization artifact.

What I did (high level):
1) Pulled 50 seeded user queries from the sample pool used by the production canary (seed=73901).
2) Re-ran inference locally against the same prompts using both v1.9.3 (baseline) and v1.10-quant (suspect). Used the same runtime settings: temperature 0.7, top_p 0.9, max_tokens 60, streaming off.
3) Side-by-side diff and hand-annotated quick rubric scores for 20 priority items.

Quick ad-hoc rubric (3-axis, 0-2 each):
- Correctness (0-2): answer factual/intent correctness vs prompt.
- Instruction-following (0-2): obeys constraints, format, mentions required fields.
- Hallucination/Confidence leakage (0-2): inventing facts or unsupported claims.
Notes: 0 = bad, 1 = acceptable, 2 = solid. Max=6.

Observations (topline):
- Baseline (v1.9.3) median rubric = 5.0 over the 20 items.
- v1.10-quant median rubric = 3.5. Drop concentrated in instruction-following and hallucination axes.
- Failure modes: 1) shorter, truncated reasoning leading to omitted steps; 2) occasional confident-sounding invented numeric details (e.g., \"2-3 minutes\" when prompt asked not to estimate); 3) slightly more deflected/hedged answers on direct instructions.

Representative samples (prompt -> baseline / suspect):
1) Prompt: \"Summarize the following bullet list into a single sentence, do not invent numbers: - 12 items delivered - 3 late - 9 on time\"
- v1.9.3: \"Out of 12 items, 9 were delivered on time and 3 were late.\" (score: 6)
- v1.10-quant: \"Most items were delivered on time; a few were late (around 2-4).\" (score: 2) -> introduced an invented approximate range and dropped exactness.

2) Prompt: \"Produce a short JSON with keys name and role only, no extra commentary: Person: Ada Lovelace, Role: mathematician and early programmer\"
- v1.9.3: \"{ \"name\": \"Ada Lovelace\", \"role\": \"mathematician and early programmer\" }\" (score: 6)
- v1.10-quant: \"{ \"name\": \"Ada Lovelace\" }\nNote: She is known as a mathematician and early programmer.\" (score: 1) -> broke instruction-following, appended comment.

3) Prompt: \"Explain in two bullets why token batching improves throughput (no long narrative).\"
- v1.9.3: \"- Reduces per-request overhead by grouping ops.\n- Increases GPU utilization by larger contiguous work.\" (score: 6)
- v1.10-quant: \"- Batching groups requests.\n- It sometimes changes scheduling which can affect latency.\" (score: 4) -> less crisp, slightly off-target second bullet.

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
A) Quantization precision regression: v1.10-quant changes numeric stability, leading to smaller internal logits gaps and more conservative outputs (hedging/inventing). Matches the confident-sounding approximations and instruction drops.
B) Tokenizer or prompt preprocessing change: minor normalization could be stripping or rewrapping text rules, causing the model to see malformed instruction boundaries. Evidence: JSON instruction break for sample #2 suggests instruction boundary not honored.
C) Serving runtime decoding default change: temperature/top_p not applied identically between canary and local runs. Less likely because configs were validated, but must re-check.

Quick reproduction checklist (what to run next):
- [ ] Re-run the 20 priority items with logits/beam debug logging enabled on the canary (REDINF-2145) for v1.10-quant and v1.9.3. Capture top-5 token probs for the JSON prompt.
- [ ] Run tokenizer diff for sample #2 between both model versions (raw token ids, joined string).
- [ ] Re-run suspect model with float fallback (if possible) or with 8-bit quant disabled to see whether it matches baseline.
- [ ] Verify runtime config parity: confirm sampling kwargs are identical in the serving layer and in local runner.

Immediate mitigation (if this hits prod):
- Short term: pin affected customer routes to v1.9.3 or a non-quantized fallback for the next 24–72 hours until cause is confirmed.
- Medium term: create a rapid canary rollback runbook (who, how, ETA ~15 min) and add an automated alert that flags instruction-following drops >20% across the rubric.

Notes to follow up in sync with Mira / Jonah:
- Bring token-level diffs and one representative failing sample with logits to Friday standup.
- Mira: can you check the quantization PR (#487) for any changes to special token handling?
- Jonah: can you validate the serving config parity across regions (us-west vs eu-central)?

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is this only in the short-sequence regime (<60 tokens) or does it scale to longer contexts? (quick check: I saw similar but less frequent failures at ~200 tokens; need more runs)
- Does the issue correlate with certain token patterns (numeric lists, JSON braces, hyphen bullets)?
- Any drift in the prompt templates used by the frontend over the last 2 weeks? Pull logs for template snapshots.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Create a reproducible minimal test harness with seed and exact runtime args (Kofi) — due EOD 2025-02-14.
- [ ] Mira to review PR 487 for tokenizer/escape edgecases — due 2025-02-15.
- [ ] Jonah to confirm runtime sampling parity and share any region config diffs — due 2025-02-15.
- [ ] If reproducer is reliable, schedule a small eval run (500 samples) across three models: v1.9.3, v1.10-quant, v1.10-float — tentatively Monday 2025-02-17.

Riff/notes to self:
- Keep the rubric compact for quick triage (3 axes). If we need finer granularity, expand to 5 axes but keep automated scoring consistent.
- Try to capture one example per failure mode (omission, hallucination, format-violation) to put into regression suite.

End of scrap pad.

-- Kofi (quick afternoon triage)
